title: Claim and resume work in a custom status queue
lead: Approval and triage agents need next's ranking and atomic claiming in configured custom queues, without placing those queues in the implementer's default pool.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing plain next's open/started pool, changing review pickup, supporting --batch with --status, or treating a custom claim as a configured in-work role.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: cmd_next currently permits only the review role in --status. The owner chose claim-in-place, own-claim resume priority, exclusion of other actors' claims, and explicit transitions limited to active destinations.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Next selection/result operations, claim operations, CLI next validation and locking, next/claim/concurrency tests, command/configuration/agent documentation.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A configured custom lane ranks by effective score with stable ties, and respects readiness, dependencies, tree/size filters and sibling work.
- Own claimed work resumes before unclaimed work; another actor's claim is skipped and reported. Read-only custom selection resolves the effective actor using existing precedence.
- --start claims in place and repeated resume changes nothing. --start-to moves to open, started or a custom status, claims atomically, and returns the resulting record.
- Unknown queues, non-review lifecycle queues, unsupported destinations, start-to without start/custom status, and batch with status fail before any mutation.
- Default/review selection and review-to-reviewing transitions retain their existing behavior. A race between sessions does not steal an intervening claim.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Permit --status for custom keys outside configured open/started/done/retired/parked/reviewing roles. The review role preserves its existing dedicated path. Reject disabled/unknown queues and name the supported choices.

Within custom selection, first rank claims belonging to the effective actor, then unclaimed items, each by effective score and queue-order ties. Skip locally foreign claims and add claimed_elsewhere entries with id and owner; retain the existing sibling skip report independently. Read-only selection uses actor configuration/environment/defaults; explicit owner retains its existing requirement for --start.

Add --start-to only with --start on a custom queue. Destination must be configured and cannot be done, retired, parked, review or reviewing; open and started roles and custom destinations are valid. Implement the claim/status change through ops with writer locking, reload and re-selection under that lock, and validation before any persistence. Do not use generic start's implicit started transition for claim-in-place. Log an actual claim/transition only; resumes do not write.

Claim-only custom pickup does not increment implementation attempts. An explicit transition to started starts one implementation attempt once; coordinate with the attempt-counting slice if already present. Document the single-queue limitation for read-only resume after changing destination.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run custom ranking, ownership, resume, transition and race tests, then full unittest discovery, tracking check, and git diff --check.

Use the project's ignored TMPDIR for temporary test fixtures, and scoped
support.isolated_discovery only for fixtures that require outside-project
discovery. The repository acceptance commands, run against the implementation
checkout's code and state, are:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json
git diff --check
```

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One reviewed implementation commit with contract docs, changelog and regenerated tracking output.
